To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Jail Inreach Project has been able to engage and link more than half of homeless inmates with mental illness with community-based health services.

the Jail Inreach Project, a case management "inreaching" program that engages homeless inmates with mental illness in establishing a plan to receive community services postrelease, has been shown to be a successful model for reducing homelessness among this population.
The Jail Inreach project, an intensive case management program, was successful in linking homeless persons with mental illness with community services.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a better understanding of the health care and behavioral health needs of homeless individuals with mental illness, and with the effectiveness of health and social services in meeting these needs.

the development and implementation of a program to address the unique needs of homeless persons with mental illness, who are incarcerated, in a manner that is consistent with their unique needs and preferences.

the development, implementation, and evaluation of the Jail Inreach Project, an innovative health care-based intensive inreach case management program designed to link homeless persons who have behavioral health problems with community health care services upon release from jail.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Jail Inreach Project participants are more successful at linking with community services postrelease than are nonproject participants.

Jail Inreach Project participants who engaged in services during incarceration and remained linked with services post-release had significantly higher rates of engagement in services and were less likely to recidivate to jail.
the Jail Inreach Project has demonstrated the ability to successfully engage homeless persons with behavioral health disorders who are incarcerated into community health services upon release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this program is an innovative, cost-effective, and promising approach to linking homeless persons with mental illness to community health services and to reducing the revolving door between the jail and the community.

we were able to engage a high proportion of homeless inmates who were referred to the program in establishing a plan of care for services postrelease, and that we were able, to some extent, to maintain linkage with these services after release.
we are able to link a majority of our participants with services, but we need more resources to ensure that the participants remain engaged with services postrelease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to link a large number of persons with services in a short period of time.

a health home-based intensive case management model can be effective in linking homeless inmates with behavioral health disorders to community health services and that the model can be replicated in other jurisdictions.
